models_evaluated: deep learning fundus photograph models trained on UK Biobank

links.outcome: Differences between development (UK Biobank) and Kenyan deployment population characteristics
links.effect: Kenyan participants were younger, likely Black/African, with higher BMI and higher prevalence of DM and hypertension than UK Biobank development population.
links.quote: Compared with the UK Biobank population used for algorithm development, participants from Kenya were younger and would probably report Black/African ethnicity, with a higher body mass index and prevalence of DM and hypertension.

links.outcome: Model performance on local Kenyan data versus development data
links.effect: MAE comparable or slightly greater; DM AUROC 0.762 (0.818 in UK Biobank); hypertension AUROC 0.765 (0.738 in UK Biobank).
links.quote: The model trained to identify DM had an area under the receiver operating curve of 0.762 (0.818 in the UK Biobank) and the hypertension model had an area under the receiver operating curve of 0.765 (0.738 in the UK Biobank).

screen.reason: This prospective validation study evaluates the external geographic and demographic generalizability of deep learning models estimating cardiovascular risk factors from retinal fundus images in Kenya, but it evaluates model performance alone without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
